page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves a strong single-core stress-ng CPU score of 2691.19, placing it in the top 25%. However, its multi-core stress-ng CPU performance of 2691.5 is weak, falling into the bottom 25%, which is expected given the low core count. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck; read-only small block cached bandwidth is poor at 129.16 GB/sec, while uncached large-block write bandwidth is also poor at 12.61 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both rank in the bottom 10%, indicating limitations under intensive transactional workloads.

Despite memory bottlenecks, single-threaded execution is stable, with average performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. LLM inference text generation using a small 135M model also registers an average speed of 78.78 tokens per second. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power or local disk storage. It is suitable for lightweight caching layers, small-scale memory-intensive applications, and basic single-threaded data processing tasks.

It operates on the KVM hypervisor with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show a strong single-core stress-ng CPU score in the top 25%, contrasted by weak multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, with both uncached write bandwidth and Redis SET operations ranking in the bottom 10%. The instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy, low-concurrency workloads. It is best suited for lightweight caching, single-threaded data processing, and small-scale memory-intensive applications.
